author: edwong57
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
  IPR036298 Chalcone isomerase superfamily (**homologous superfamily**). It maps to GO:0016872
  *intramolecular lyase activity*.

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

  | UniProtKB | Gene (SGD) | Protein |
  |---|---|---|
  | P38884 | AIM18 / FMP22 (YHR198C; SGD:S000001241) | Altered inheritance of mitochondria protein 18 |
  | P38885 | AIM46 / FMP34 (YHR199C; SGD:S000001242) | Altered inheritance of mitochondria protein 46 |

* **Description of issue**
  Follow-up to **#4437** (closed 2023-02-08). That issue cited the same paper (PMID:36739946), and
  InterPro removed the isomerase GO term from **IPR016087** (the chalcone isomerase domain entry).
  AIM18 and AIM46 still receive GO:0016872 through the related **homologous superfamily** entry
  **IPR036298** 

PMID:36739946 (abstract; SGD's reference): "Aim18p and Aim46p … adopt CHI folds, but they lack select
  active site residues and possess an extra fungal-specific loop. Consistent with these differences,
  Aim18p and Aim46p lack CHI activity and also the fatty acid-binding capabilities of other CHI-like
  proteins, but instead bind heme." The paper reports that diverse fungal homologues also bind heme.

  CHI-fold proteins include non-catalytic members: CHI-like proteins, fatty-acid-binding proteins, and
  these fungal hemoproteins. So an activity mapping at the homologous-superfamily level over-annotates.

  **Suggested fix:** remove GO:0016872 from IPR036298.
title: InterPro2GO issue: (follow-up to #4437) - IPR036298 (Chalcone isomerase superfamily) -> GO:0016872 on catalytically inactive CHI-fold hemoproteins
